newsitem.title: INDIA: OPINION-WEEKLY TECHNICAL ANALYSIS OF BOMBAY SHARE INDEX.
newsitem.headline: OPINION-WEEKLY TECHNICAL ANALYSIS OF BOMBAY SHARE INDEX.

text.p: INDEX STRONG DESPITE FALLING VALUES, ALERT FOR MINOR
BOTTOM FORMATION BETWEEN 3385-3352 is a trend analysis of the 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index for the period February 24 to 28 by analyst Mehmood Khan at Times Guaranty Financials Ltd:

Trading for the week ended on a pessimistic note, with a loss of 82.50 points (2.34 percent) at 3439.49 levels over the previous week. The market commenced the week, on a strong note, but the higher levels (33586.05) could not be maintained due to off-loading of speculative positions, triggered with indications that the petroleum price hike cannot be ruled out.

At 3433.27 levels, the sensex has corrected the rally of 269.90 points (3316.15 to 3586.05) by 56.61 percent. Since the corrective move has broken, the vital support of 50 percent, it has became eminent that the support would emerge between 66.67 percent and 80 percent retracement at 3405-3370 levels. The mechanical indicators have sighted the minor bottom formation on Monday/Tuesday that may be marginally higher than 3316.15 levels. The sensex moves into the CIT (Change In Trend) time window from February 24, 1997. It may form a down day on Monday but significant buying may emerge, thereafter which result in minor rally. The advanced indicators point to next week's close (i.e. Post-budg

With the index already in the level and time zones of turn, it is time to look into the macro patterns for any signs of reversal. A reversal has already been signalled on Friday with the formation of a hammer candlestick pattern and a fade bar which usually occurs at the end of a trend. As per the Time Logic analysis, the decline (from 3812.13) is 26 trading days old. The cluster of time logic support the bottom formation on February 24/25 1997. The minor corrective down trend from 3586.05 is four trading days old may lose momentum on February 24, 1997, the target for the downside can be placed at 3385-3352 levels.

The correctionary trend in Andhra Valley, Ashok Leyland, Ballarpur, Bajaj Auto, Bombay Dyeing, Cadbury, Century Textiles, ICICI, IDBI, IFCI, ITC Bhadra, ITC, L&T, MTNL, Mahindra & Mahindra, OBC, Raymonds Wollen, Reliance, SCICI, SBI, Sail, Sterlite, Tata Chemicals, TISCO, Tata Power, Tata Tea, United Phosphorus and Mastergain 92 are indicating losing momentum on the weekly chart. These counters may seek lower values in the initial half of the week, but may witness buying interest in due course and may probably close the week on a strong note. The best trading opportunity for the week's trading is to be on the long side from Tuesday with a stop-loss of 3315 levels.

The price following oscillators on the weekly bar chart are exhibiting positive divergence justifying that the bottom may be formed at 3385-3355 levels - Relative Strength Index (RSI) is 55.53, Price Rate of Change (ROC) is placed at 15.98, short term stochastic is hovering at 36.33 and its trigger line is at 41.72, while the medium term stochastic is 65.89 and the trigger is 66.33.

For the current week, the BSE Sensex may find support at 3405, 3385 & 3352 levels. On the higher end it may encounter resistance at 3510-3570 levels. The National Index may witness buying interest at 1469-1440 levels and resistance at 1510 & 1547 levels.
(The opinions expressed in this article reflect the views of the author only. They should not be taken as reflecting the views of Reuters.)
